user_goal: Browse a two-level category tree — land on a parent category, see what types sit under it, drill into a subcategory, and still reach a product whose category moved via its old link.
business_goal: Make the catalog's hierarchy crawlable and answerable (breadcrumbs, canonical, FAQ/CollectionPage markup, sitemap, llms.txt) while never 404ing an indexed or shared product URL after a re-parent.

user_journey.step: See subcategory tiles with rolled-up counts and answer-first intro copy
Read the category FAQ accordion below the grid
Drill into a thin child category
Jump back up or across via the sibling row
Follow an old product link whose category moved
Land on the product at its canonical URL with a 4-level breadcrumb
Discover the tree from the header mega-menu or the mobile drawer
Machine surfaces expose the same tree

happy_path.action: Navigate to the parent category page /products/marketing-prints
happy_path.expected_result: HTTP 200; h1 'Marketing Prints' renders even though direct_product_count is 0

happy_path.action: Read the document title, meta description and canonical link
happy_path.expected_result: title 'Marketing Prints – Flyers, Posters & More | Urgent Printers' (from meta_title); description equals the category's meta_description; canonical is <SITE_URL>/products/marketing-prints; no robots meta (indexable)

happy_path.action: Read the answer-first intro paragraph under the h1
happy_path.selector: text 'Marketing prints are printed promotional materials'
happy_path.expected_result: seo_intro renders above the product grid as prose, not the plain category description
Home (sr-only label) > All Products > Marketing Prints, with 'Marketing Prints' as the non-linked current page
3 ListItems: Home, All Products, Marketing Prints — names and order identical to the visible breadcrumb, items absolute on SITE_URL

happy_path.action: Check the subcategory tiles block above the product grid
happy_path.selector: nav[aria-label='Marketing Prints subcategories'] containing heading 'Shop Marketing Prints by type'
happy_path.expected_result: Two tiles — 'Flyers & Leaflets' linking /products/flyers-leaflets and 'Posters' linking /products/posters — each with its rolled-up count rendered as '1 product' (singular)

happy_path.action: Check the product grid rolls descendants up into the parent
happy_path.expected_result: Both descendant products are listed — 'A5 Flyers' (child flyers-leaflets) and 'A2 Posters' (child posters) — despite the parent owning no products directly
numberOfItems 2; itemListElement URLs are the products' own canonical child-category paths (/products/posters/a2-posters, /products/flyers-leaflets/a5-flyers); description equals the meta description

happy_path.action: Scroll to the category FAQ accordion below the grid and expand the first question
happy_path.selector: h2#category-faq-heading 'Marketing Prints FAQs'; details > summary 'What sizes do you print?'
happy_path.expected_result: Accordion renders 2 questions; expanding the first reveals the answer 'Sizes < 5 inch and > 3 inch are available as custom cuts, alongside standard A6 to A3.' — the raw '<' and '>' survive as prose and are not stripped as markup

happy_path.action: Read the FAQPage JSON-LD and compare to the visible accordion
happy_path.expected_result: 2 Question entries whose name/acceptedAnswer.text match the visible summary/answer text exactly, including the '< 5 inch and > 3 inch' clause (no markup-only FAQ)
Navigates to /products/posters and the child category page renders

happy_path.action: On the child page, check the breadcrumb includes the parent and the sibling row renders
happy_path.selector: nav[aria-label=Breadcrumb]; nav[aria-label='Related categories'] heading 'More from Marketing Prints'
happy_path.expected_result: Breadcrumb Home > All Products > Marketing Prints > Posters; a 'Shop all Marketing Prints' pill plus a 'Flyers & Leaflets' sibling pill

alternate_paths.path_name: Thin child category is crawlable but not indexable

steps.action: Load /products/posters and read its robots meta and canonical
steps.expected_result: robots content 'noindex, follow' (1 rolled-up product < MIN_INDEXABLE_SUBCATEGORY_PRODUCTS = 3); canonical still self-referential <SITE_URL>/products/posters; title 'Posters | Urgent Printers'

steps.action: Read the child page's BreadcrumbList JSON-LD
steps.expected_result: 4 ListItems: Home, All Products, Marketing Prints, Posters — i.e. the ancestor chain comes from the API's ancestors array, not from the URL (which is flat)

steps.action: Click 'Shop all Marketing Prints' in the sibling row
steps.expected_result: Returns to /products/marketing-prints

alternate_paths.path_name: Parent that also owns a direct product shows both levels

steps.action: Load /products/stickers-labels (1 direct product + 1 child)
steps.expected_result: HTTP 200; h1 'Stickers & Labels'; no robots noindex (root categories are never 'thin')

steps.action: Check the subcategory tile and the grid together
steps.expected_result: A 'Die-cut Stickers' tile is present AND the grid lists both the direct product 'test' and the descendant 'Custom Die-Cut Stickers' — rollup does not hide the parent's own product

alternate_paths.path_name: A moved product's old URL 308s to its canonical path

steps.action: Request the old URL /products/stickers-labels/custom-diecut-stickers without following redirects
steps.expected_result: HTTP 308 with Location /products/die-cut-stickers/custom-diecut-stickers (permanentRedirect, not a 200-then-client-redirect)

steps.action: Follow to the canonical PDP and read the breadcrumb
steps.expected_result: Home > All Products > Stickers & Labels > Die-cut Stickers > Custom Die-Cut Stickers; BreadcrumbList JSON-LD has the same 5 names in the same order

steps.action: Read the Product JSON-LD on the canonical PDP
steps.expected_result: category is the full path string 'Stickers & Labels > Die-cut Stickers'; sku 16; url on the die-cut-stickers segment

steps.action: Read the PDP canonical link
steps.expected_result: <SITE_URL>/products/die-cut-stickers/custom-diecut-stickers — the new segment, so the 308 target and the canonical agree

alternate_paths.path_name: Header mega-menu and mobile drawer expose the 2-level tree

steps.action: At desktop width, open the header 'Shop' panel
steps.expected_result: Panel opens (aria-expanded true) showing 'Shop by occasion'; 'Marketing Prints' appears as a top-level entry with 'Flyers & Leaflets' and 'Posters' nested beneath it, and 'Stickers & Labels' with 'Die-cut Stickers' nested

steps.action: At 375px width, open the mobile drawer and expand a parent row
steps.selector: button[aria-label='Open menu']; button[aria-label='Show Marketing Prints subcategories']
steps.expected_result: Drawer opens; the toggle flips to aria-label 'Hide Marketing Prints subcategories' and reveals indented child rows 'Flyers & Leaflets' and 'Posters'

alternate_paths.path_name: Discovery surfaces that must stay top-level only

steps.action: On the homepage, inspect the 'All Categories' rail
steps.expected_result: Only the 6 root categories appear (Banners & Flex, Business Cards, Mugs & Promotional, Stickers & Labels, T-Shirts & Apparel, Marketing Prints); no child tile for Flyers & Leaflets, Posters or Die-cut Stickers

steps.action: On /search with no query, inspect the 'Browse by Category' grid
steps.selector: h2 'Browse by Category' and the link grid under it
steps.expected_result: Same 6 root categories only — getRootCategories filters children out

steps.action: On a listing page, inspect the sidebar Category filter
steps.expected_result: Children appear under their parent with visual indentation (nestCategories depth 1), e.g. Flyers & Leaflets and Posters immediately after Marketing Prints

steps.action: Scan every product card on the homepage for repeats
steps.expected_result: No product appears in two shelves — a rolled-up parent shelf and a child shelf never both carry the same product (dedupeShelfProducts)

steps.action: Fetch /sitemap.xml and inspect the <loc> set
steps.expected_result: Includes /products/marketing-prints; EXCLUDES the thin subcategories /products/flyers-leaflets, /products/posters, /products/die-cut-stickers; but still lists their products /products/flyers-leaflets/a5-flyers, /products/posters/a2-posters, /products/die-cut-stickers/custom-diecut-stickers

steps.action: Fetch /robots.txt
steps.expected_result: HTTP 200 text/plain; allows / for '*' and for the AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended); disallows /cart, /checkout, /account, /auth, /api/, /proof-approval/; declares the sitemap URL

steps.action: Fetch /llms.txt
steps.expected_result: HTTP 200 text/plain starting '# Urgent Printers'; lists Marketing Prints with its description under '## Shop'; omits the thin subcategories; '- Phone: +91 95281 91807' under '## Contact'; ends with the Sitemap line

steps.action: Check the footer and /contact phone numbers against the SEO constant
steps.expected_result: Both render '+91 95281 91807' (CONTACT_PHONE_DISPLAY) with the footer anchor href 'tel:+919528191807' — same number llms.txt and the Organization JSON-LD advertise

alternate_paths.path_name: Suspense skeleton replaces the deleted loading.tsx files

steps.action: Confirm no loading.tsx exists anywhere under app/products/ and the listing skeleton comes from the page's own Suspense boundary
steps.selector: filesystem app/products/**/loading.tsx; ProductListingBodySkeleton inside <Suspense> in app/products/[categorySlug]/page.tsx
steps.expected_result: Zero loading.tsx files under app/products/ (deliberate — a route-level loading shell flushes HTTP 200 before notFound()/permanentRedirect() can set the status); the skeleton renders inside the page instead, which is what keeps alt-06's 308 and err-01/err-02's 404 real status codes

error_paths.trigger: Request a category slug that does not exist: /products/nope-category
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Real HTTP 404 (not a soft 404 with status 200) and the not-found page; notFound() runs in CategoryPage before the Suspense boundary

error_paths.trigger: Request a valid product under a category segment that is not a known category: /products/bogus-cat/custom-diecut-stickers
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Real HTTP 404 — isKnownCategorySlug rejects the junk segment so it cannot mint a cached 308 for every random prefix

error_paths.trigger: Add a facet param to an indexable category URL: /products/marketing-prints?sort=price_asc
error_paths.expected_ui_response: robots 'noindex, follow' and canonical collapsing back to the bare <SITE_URL>/products/marketing-prints

error_paths.trigger: Submit a search from a category page: /products/marketing-prints?q=flyers
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Redirect to /products?q=flyers (the Typesense endpoint cannot be category-scoped, so the page hands off rather than silently ignoring the category)

error_paths.trigger: Apply an unrecognised value to the sort facet: /products/marketing-prints?sort=bogus (and ?sort=price_asc, the underscore spelling of a real value)
error_paths.expected_ui_response: The invalid value is ignored and the listing renders the same products as the bare category page — NOT 'No products found'. Regression guard for a real defect found by this run: lib/api/products.ts forwarded an unmapped sort as the literal string sort_by=undefined, the backend 422'd, getProducts swallowed it and the page served an empty grid at HTTP 200. Fixed with parseSortParam.

error_paths.trigger: Apply an unrecognised value to the badge facet: /products/marketing-prints?badge=bogus (and ?badge=toString, to check the prototype-chain case)
error_paths.expected_ui_response: The invalid value is ignored and the listing renders the same products as the bare category page. Same defect class as err-05 on the other first-class facet in FACET_PARAMS; fixed with parseBadgeParam. ?badge=sale must still reach the backend as on_sale=true, so its empty result on this category stays legitimate rather than being papered over.

edge_cases.case: Parent category with zero direct products still renders a full page
edge_cases.existing_validation: CategoryPage only notFound()s on a missing/inactive category, never on an empty one; getProducts is called with categorySlug and the backend rolls descendants up
edge_cases.risk_note: Marketing Prints (direct_product_count 0, product_count 2) is exactly this case — a regression to exact-match filtering would render an empty parent page that still looks 200 OK

edge_cases.case: Thin-subcategory noindex is computed client-side from productCount, not read from the API's noindex flag
edge_cases.existing_validation: isCategoryIndexable in lib/seo/category.ts: isActive !== false && noindex !== true && productCount > 0 && !isThinCategory
edge_cases.risk_note: The API returns noindex:false for Posters, yet the page must still emit noindex because its rolled-up count is 1 (< 3). The two mechanisms are independent and both must hold; asserting only the API field would pass while the page was wrong

edge_cases.case: FAQ answer prose contains bare '<' and '>' characters
edge_cases.existing_validation: toPlainText strips only real tags via /<\/?[a-zA-Z][^>]*>/g and block breaks; bare comparison operators are preserved
edge_cases.risk_note: A naive strip-all-angle-brackets sanitiser would silently mangle 'Sizes < 5 inch and > 3 inch' in both the visible answer and the FAQPage JSON-LD; the two must still match each other exactly or the markup is non-compliant

edge_cases.case: SSR text interpolation splits heading strings with HTML comments
edge_cases.existing_validation: None needed — React streaming emits 'Shop <!-- -->Marketing Prints<!-- --> by type' and 'Marketing Prints<!-- --> FAQs' in the raw HTML
edge_cases.risk_note: A raw-HTML substring assertion on those headings fails even though the page is correct; assert via the DOM/accessible text (Playwright getByRole/getByText), not against the HTTP response body

edge_cases.case: Two <nav> landmarks on a parent page share the accessible name '<Parent> subcategories'
edge_cases.existing_validation: None at plan time — CategoryChipBar's row nav used aria-label={row.label} and SubcategoryTiles used aria-label={`${parent.name} subcategories`}, producing the same string
edge_cases.risk_note: Confirmed live and FIXED during this run: axe 'landmark-unique' (moderate, 1 node on each of /products/marketing-prints and /products/stickers-labels, and on no other page). The tiles nav now uses aria-labelledby pointing at its own 'Shop <Parent> by type' heading and the chip row reads '<Parent> subcategory filters'. The specs still locate the tiles block by its heading rather than its aria-label, so they are label-rename-proof either way

edge_cases.case: No loading.tsx under app/products/ by design
edge_cases.existing_validation: Guarded by tests/subcategories.test.ts and documented in the frontend CLAUDE.md 'Key known fixes' table
edge_cases.risk_note: Re-adding one flushes a 200 shell before notFound()/permanentRedirect(), turning alt-06's 308 and err-01/err-02's 404 into soft-200s — the exact regression the deletion of three loading.tsx files was meant to prevent

edge_cases.case: Canonical/JSON-LD origin comes from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, which is http://localhost:3000 in this dev environment
edge_cases.existing_validation: resolveSiteUrl in lib/seo/site.ts falls back to https://urgentprinters.com only when the env var is not a valid http(s) origin
edge_cases.risk_note: Assertions must compare against the running origin, not a hardcoded production host, or they fail for the wrong reason locally and pass for the wrong reason in prod

edge_cases.case: Moving a product back to its old category can create a redirect loop for visitors who cached the 308
edge_cases.existing_validation: Documented in a code comment in app/products/[categorySlug]/[productSlug]/page.tsx; canonicalProductPath returns null when segments already match so the server itself cannot loop
edge_cases.risk_note: Server-side is loop-safe, but browser-cached 308s are not revocable — product 16 must not be moved back. This is why this run is read-only against the category/product data

edge_cases.case: getCategories() swallows backend errors into an empty array
edge_cases.existing_validation: The PDP throws 'Categories unavailable; cannot validate stale category slug' rather than 404ing, and app/sitemap.ts throws 'catalog unavailable' and falls back to static entries
edge_cases.risk_note: Correct handling, but it means a backend outage during capture surfaces as a 500 / short sitemap rather than an obvious API failure — check the backend is up before treating either as an app defect

edge_cases.case: Homepage shelf splitting activates only when a root holds >= 60% of the catalog
edge_cases.existing_validation: DOMINANT_SHARE = 0.6 with a >= 2 non-empty children requirement in planShelfCategories; dedupeShelfProducts is the defensive backstop
edge_cases.risk_note: With this dev catalog (9 products spread over 6 roots) no root is dominant, so the child-promotion branch is latent and only dedupeShelfProducts is actually exercised by alt-15

edge_cases.case: Category pages are ISR-cached (revalidate = 60) and generateStaticParams pre-enumerates every category slug
edge_cases.existing_validation: export const revalidate = 60 on both the category page and the PDP; the PDP returns [] from generateStaticParams deliberately to avoid bursting the backend rate limiter in dev
edge_cases.risk_note: A capture run immediately after a data change can read up to 60s-stale HTML; first visits to a PDP compile and fetch on demand, so the first navigation is slow enough to need a generous timeout

gaps: The feature's own plan document (plans/subcategories-seo-plan.md) describes the PRODUCTION taxonomy (Wedding > Wedding Tags etc.). The dev catalog this run tests is a different, smaller tree (Marketing Prints > Flyers & Leaflets / Posters; Stickers & Labels > Die-cut Stickers). Plan steps are grounded in the live dev data, not that document.
Admin-side authoring of parent_id, seo_intro, seo_body and faqs is out of scope for this --app=frontend run; the storefront is tested against data already present in the dev DB and makes no writes.

Only one of the plan document's two depth levels exists in dev data — there is no depth-3 category, so buildCategoryTree's MAX_NAV_DEPTH = 3 headroom and the depth-2-cap enforcement are not exercised end to end here.
No category in the dev catalog has seo_body set, so CategorySeoBody's long-form prose branch renders only its FAQ half; the paragraphs branch is covered by unit tests only.

No category has google_product_category set or noindex = true in dev, so the admin-flagged-noindex branch of isCategoryIndexable and the feed's google_product_category passthrough are not covered by this run.

No indexable subcategory exists in dev data (all three children have 1 rolled-up product, below the threshold of 3), so 'a child category that IS in the sitemap' has no live fixture — creating one would mean re-parenting real products, which this run is explicitly forbidden from doing.
Pagination of a rolled-up parent listing (?page=2, and the isFirstPage suppression of seo_body/FAQs) cannot be exercised: the largest category holds 3 products against a PAGE_SIZE of 12.
